kind.label: Note type
kind.enc_d: Locked in your browser. Only people with the full link can read it. The link is long, because the key is in it.
kind.basic_d: Readable on the server, so its link can be a name you choose. Not for secrets.
convert.text_enc: Only people with the full link can read it. You can make it basic: its text is then readable on the server and its link can have a name.
convert.text_basic: The server can read it. You can encrypt it: it is locked in your browser and only the full link opens it.
convert.confirm_enc: Make this note encrypted? It will be locked in your browser. Anyone who opens a link without the key (#k=…) will not be able to read it, so share the full link again. Version history is cleared.
convert.confirm_basic: Make this note basic? Its text will be stored readable on the server, and anyone with a link can read it. Version history is cleared.
convert.need_key: Open the full owner link (with the key) to change the type of this note.
err.convert_same: The note is already of that type.
err.convert_blocked: A note with {what} can’t change type yet. Make a copy instead.
err.slug_basic_only: Only a basic note can have a link name. An encrypted note keeps the long link, because its key is in it.
sum.private: Encrypted: only the full link opens it; we can’t read it.
sum.public: Basic: the server can read it, and so can anyone with a link.
new.public_note: Basic note: the server can read it, and so can anyone with a link. Use Encrypted for anything private. What does that mean?
status.public: Basic note: anyone with the address can read it, and so can the server.
faq.public_a: A note you create as “Basic”. It isn’t encrypted: the server can read it, anyone with a link can read it, and it can be fetched as plain text with /raw/. In return its link can be a name you choose and rename, like /monday-meeting. Use it for things meant to be shared. Search engines never list it. The owner can change a note between basic and encrypted later, from the share dialog. Some features only work with basic notes: your public page, the mock API and SSH.
about.lead: An encrypted note is locked in your browser before it’s saved. The key that opens it is part of the link you share, so we can’t read it: only people with the link can. A basic note is readable instead, and its link can be a name you choose. Questions? See the FAQ.
meta.desc_new: Notes you can share, basic or end-to-end encrypted. The server can’t read the encrypted ones.
about.s3t: We can’t read an encrypted note; we only know your rules, like when it should disappear.
err.profile_public: Only basic notes saved in your account can be on your profile.
ex.profile: List this basic note on your page /@your-name.
faq.mock_a: A basic note that contains JSON (the whole text or a ```json block) is served at /mock/LINK, with paths like /mock/LINK/users/0 and open CORS, for prototypes.
faq.page_a: Basic notes saved in your account can be listed on /@your-name by turning on “Show on my public page”. Only view-only links are shown.
faq.raw_a: Basic notes can be fetched as plain text, e.g. curl https://your-domain/raw/note-name. Encrypted notes can’t: the server doesn’t have the key.
faq.ssh_a: If the server has it turned on, ssh -p 2222 your-domain < note.md creates a basic note (kept 30 days) and ssh -p 2222 your-domain get LINK prints one. Basic notes only.
faq.limits_a: Anyone with the full link can open the note, so treat the link like a password. Images from other websites aren’t loaded, so readers don’t leak to them. Features marked as basic, or ones that receive text from other apps, mean the server sees that text.
privacy.s1: The text, titles and files of encrypted notes. They are locked in your browser; the key is in your link and never reaches us.
privacy.s5: Basic notes, SSH, the mock API, the inbox and the Telegram bot mean the server sees that text. They are marked in the app and explained in the FAQ.
profile.off: Off. Basic notes can be listed on your page /@{name}.
rule.profile_public: Only basic notes saved in your account can be on your public page.
terms.s3: We may remove a note or turn off a link when we learn it breaks these terms or the law, for example a basic note used for phishing. Because we can’t read encrypted notes, we act on the link that was reported.
warn.public_keys: This basic note contains a private link or attachment key (#k=… or nh-file:…). Anyone who can read this note could open those too. Continue anyway?
new.slug_warn: Careful: an easy-to-guess name with “{mode}” access. People still need the full link, with its key, to change the note.
privacy.lead: We built NoteHop so we can’t read your encrypted notes. Basic notes are readable on purpose, so they are marked as such. Here is what we do keep, and why.
rule.burn_block_e2e: Self-destructing blocks only work on encrypted notes.
rule.password_e2e: A password only works on encrypted notes. Choose “Encrypted” first.
terms.lead: The short version: use NoteHop for lawful things, keep your links safe, and know that we can’t read encrypted notes (basic notes are stored readable).
terms.s2: Your notes stay yours. Encrypted notes are locked in your browser, so we can’t read, check or recover them; basic notes are stored readable. You’re responsible for what you write and who you give links to.
faq.what_a: A place to write a note and share it with a link. You decide what people with the link can do: read it, write with you, reply, tick a list, or suggest changes. A note is either encrypted (the default) or basic: encrypted notes are locked in your browser, basic notes are readable on the server and can have a link name you choose.
faq.encrypt_q: How is an encrypted note kept private?
faq.sees_a: For an encrypted note: not your text, titles or file contents. It does see what it needs to enforce your choices: when a note was made and changed, its size, link permissions, expiry, how many times it was opened, which boxes are ticked and how many votes a poll has (not the labels), and IP addresses for abuse limits. A basic note is different: the server can read it.
faq.lost_a: No, and that’s on purpose: for an encrypted note the key to open it is only in the link, so we never have it. Sign in to keep your links in your account, or save your owner link somewhere safe. A basic note is easy to find again by its link name.
home.lead: Write, send the link, done. By default your note is locked in your browser before it's saved, so not even we can read it. Or make it a basic note, with a link name you choose.
home.title: Notes you share with a link
privacy.s2: Locked notes, basic notes (readable by the server), link permissions, times, how often a note was opened, ticks and poll counts, and, if you have an account, your username and an encrypted list of your notes.
